title: Workplace Access, Change, and Global Travel Playbook
author: Leah Kim
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates company-wide policies and step-by-step procedures for: access and permissions (entitlement lifecycle), change management, data handling and classification, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, and global travel. It is intended for requesters, approvers, line managers, and process owners. The document includes practical templates and runnable examples for frequently used workflows.

Scope and applicability:

- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and approved external vendors.
- Covers systems and services under Redwood control, including cloud accounts, internal admin consoles, payroll/expense systems, and external vendor portals when acting on Redwood’s behalf.
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks (see related pages).

Owners and escalation:

- Primary owner: People Ops (policy maintenance, approvals cadence).
- Access control steward: Security & Compliance (RBAC design, periodic audits).
- Procurement owner: Finance & Legal (PO policy, vendor contracts).
- Travel owner: People Ops (policy, corporate card governance).
- Escalation path: requestor -> direct manager -> owner_team contact -> People Ops director.

1) Access & Permissions (Entitlement Lifecycle)

Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access while enabling productive work.

Roles and definitions:

- Requestor: employee requiring access.
- Approver: direct manager or role owner.
- Role Owner: team or service owner responsible for role definitions (e.g., "infra-admin", "billing-reader").
- Provisioning system: Identity Provider (IdP) + SCIM automation feeding our access orchestration service.

Entitlement matrix (summary):

- Day-to-day access (<= 30 days): Manager approval required. Examples: temporary dev credentials, test cluster access.
- Project access (> 30 days): Manager + Role Owner sign-off. Examples: service-specific production access.
- Admin-level access: Manager + Role Owner + Security approval. Examples: core infra, secrets-management admin.
- Vendor/contractor access: Manager + Security + Procurement (term-limited).

Request workflow (standard):

1. Requestor files an Access Request via the Access Portal (template below).
2. Automated check: IdP verifies group mappings; if matching policy, auto-approve for low-risk roles.
3. Manager receives approval email with 48-hour SLA to approve/deny.
4. If Role Owner approval required, routed to them after manager approval.
5. Provisioning automation grants access and records audit event (SAML/SCIM).
6. Access review occurs at 90-day cadence for all non-service accounts; owners must certify access or trigger revocation.

Emergency access (break-glass):

- Use the emergency escalation channel with multifactor confirmation (Slack private channel + ticket).
- Emergency admin sessions are limited to 4 hours and must be logged; postmortem required within 48 hours.

Example Access Request template (JSON payload for automation):

{
  "requester_email": "alice@example.com",
  "requested_role": "service-readonly",
  "justification": "Onboarding for analytics project",
  "duration": "90d",
  "manager_approval": "pending"
}

2) Change Management

Purpose: Reduce risk while enabling regular changes to services, infra, and policy.

Change types and approvals:

- Standard change: Pre-authorized, repeatable, low-risk (no CAB). Owner: service team. Examples: scheduled library upgrades per policy.
- Normal change: Requires Change Advisory Board (CAB) review for medium/high risk. Owner: service team + change manager.
- Emergency change: Go-to state for outages or critical fixes. Owner: incident commander; post-implementation review mandatory.

CAB composition and meeting cadence:

- Weekly CAB for scheduled normal changes. Members: Change Manager, 2 SRE reps, 1 Security rep, Finance/Compliance as needed.
- Emergency CAB: ad-hoc with rota-defined on-call staff.

Change submission checklist (minimum):

- Change ID and owner
- Rollout window and blackout windows
- Backout/rollback plan with exact commands or scripts
- Monitoring & verification steps (metrics to observe)
- Impacted services and stakeholders
- Test plan or pre-production verification evidence

Rollback template (example commands):

- Step 1: Halt rollout: ./deploy stop --change-id CHG-2025-1234
- Step 2: Revert to last good artifact: ./deploy revert --artifact v2025.01
- Step 3: Verify service health via: curl -fsS https://status.internal/service/health || echo "health-fail"

3) Data Management and Classification

Classification tiers:

- Public: Data safe for external distribution.
- Internal: Company-only, non-sensitive operational data.
- Confidential: Customer PII, model training datasets with contractual restrictions. Access requires documented business justification and DPA alignment.
- Restricted: Secrets, private keys, and regulated data. Access is strictly controlled and audited.

Data access request flow:

1. Request submitted to Data Catalog (include dataset, purpose, and retention).
2. Data steward reviews classification and returns decision within 5 business days.
3. For Confidential/Restricted data, Security performs a privacy review and approves technical controls.

Retention and deletion:

- Default retention for internal logs: 90 days.
- Product telemetry: 365 days unless otherwise specified.
- Customer data: per contract; default 30 days post-termination unless extended by customer agreement.
- Data deletion requests must produce a deletion certificate stored with the ticket.

Storage and encryption requirements:

- All Confidential/Restricted datasets must be stored encrypted at rest with KMS-managed keys.
- Secrets must be stored in approved Secrets Manager only.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Thresholds and approvals (summary):

- <= $2,000: Manager approval.
- $2,001 - $25,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- > $25,000: Manager + Finance + Legal (contract review) + Procurement team.

Preferred vendors and purchase channel:

- Use the Procurement Portal for all SaaS subscriptions and hardware purchases.
- Use approved vendor list (AVL) maintained by Procurement - exceptions require Procurement approval.

Purchase Order (PO) process (steps):

1. Requestor fills Purchase Request template in Procurement Portal (fields below).
2. Finance validates budget availability and routes to Legal for contract review if > $25k.
3. Procurement issues PO; vendor must acknowledge before order.

Purchase Request template (fields):

- project_code
- vendor_name
- business_justification
- estimated_amount
- requested_delivery_date
- approver_manager

Expense reimbursement guidelines:

- Use Concur for expense submissions. Attach receipts > $25 and itemize airfare and hotel nights.
- Meal per diem: $75/day domestic; regional caps for international (see Travel section).
- Corporate card: allowed for travel-related expenses; reconcile within 7 business days.

Example PO JSON (automation-friendly):

{
  "project_code": "ENG-PLATFORM-Q2",
  "vendor_name": "FastInfra Inc",
  "amount": "12000",
  "description": "Dedicated support contract"
}

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding

Onboarding checklist:

1. Procurement issues initial SOW/PO.
2. Legal & Security complete vendor risk assessment (VRM questionnaire).
3. Finance verifies payment terms and tax forms.
4. Security (if access required) defines least-privilege access and term-limits.
5. Procurement adds vendor to AVL and assigns vendor owner.

Vendor re-assessment cadence:

- High-risk vendors: quarterly review.
- Medium-risk vendors: semi-annual.
- Low-risk vendors: annual.

Security controls required for vendors with system access:

- Unique vendor accounts (no shared generic logins).
- MFA enabled on all vendor accounts.
- Access timeboxes (e.g., 30/90 days) and automated expiry.
- Contract clause for data handling, breach notification (72 hours), and audit rights.

6) Global Travel Policy

Booking and approvals:

- Domestic travel: Manager approval required for trips longer than 2 consecutive nights or > $1,000 total.
- International travel: Manager + People Ops travel approval; certain countries require Security clearance (see Travel Restrictions matrix).
- Use corporate travel portal or approved travel agencies; exceptions require People Ops pre-approval.

Per diems and allowable expenses:

- Domestic per diem: $75/day for meals & incidentals.
- International per diem: determined by country band (see appendix table).
- Ground transportation: rideshare or taxi; use lowest-cost safe option.

Safety and emergency procedures:

- All travelers must register trip in the Travel Tracker and share itinerary with People Ops.
- Emergency contact: People Ops on-call + Security on-call.
- Medical evacuations: covered for business travel with corporate insurance when pre-approved.

Travel Restrictions matrix (examples):

- High-risk jurisdictions: require Security clearance and written approval from People Ops director.
- Sanctioned countries: travel is prohibited unless Legal provides specific written exception.

Expense claim timeline:

- Submit expense reports within 10 business days of trip completion. Delays > 30 days require manager justification.

7) Templates and Quick Artifacts

Included templates (accessible in Templates library):

- Access Request (web form + JSON payload)
- Purchase Request (Procurement Portal template + PO JSON sample)
- Vendor Onboarding checklist (CSV checklist)
- Change Request form (CAB submission HTML form)
- Travel Authorization form (pre-travel approval fields)

Access Request sample (web form fields):

- requester_name
- requester_email
- system_or_dataset
- requested_role
- justification
- duration

Purchase Request sample (CSV header):

project_code,vendor_name,amount,requested_by,manager_approver,finance_approval
ENG-PLATFORM-Q2,FastInfra Inc,12000,leah.kim@example.com,marcus.nguyen@example.com,pending

Change Request quick checklist (bullet list for CAB submission):

- CHG-Id assigned
- Owner and rollback owner listed
- Verified pre-prod test results attached
- Monitoring metric thresholds listed

Appendix: contacts and SLAs

- People Ops (policy inbox): people-ops@redwood.ai (SLA: 3 business days for policy questions)
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai (SLA: 2 business days on purchase requests)
- Security/Access steward: security-ops@redwood.ai (SLA: 5 business days for non-emergency access reviews)
- Emergency change channel: #emergency-changes (instant)

Revision history:

- 2024-11-15: Initial published version (Leah Kim)
- 2025-02-10: Updated procurement thresholds and travel per-diem bands (Leah Kim)

Related resources and links:

- Source of truth for templates: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates

Feedback and updates:

Submit feedback using the doc comment feature or email people-ops@redwood.ai. Major policy changes require cross-functional review and an approval from the People Ops director and one representative each from Security and Finance.
